segments: . On the occasion, compare

. The Psalm illustrates true repentance, in which are comprised conviction, confession, sorrow, prayer for mercy, and purposes of amendment, and it is accompanied by a lively faith. 
 
    1-4. A plea for mercy is a confession of guilt. 
 
    blot out--as from a register. 
 
    transgressions--literally, "rebellions" (

entries.title: Psalms 51:2
segments: 2. Wash me--Purity as well as pardon is desired by true penitents.

entries.title: Psalms 51:3
segments: 3. For ... before me--Conviction precedes forgiveness; and, as a gift of God, is a plea for it (

entries.title: Psalms 51:4
segments:
4. Against thee--chiefly, and as sins against others are violations of God's law, in one sense only. 
 
    that ... judgest--that is, all palliation of his crime is excluded; it is the design in making this confession to recognize God's justice, however severe the sentence.

entries.title: Psalms 51:5
segments: 5, 6. His guilt was aggravated by his essential, native sinfulness, which is as contrary to God's requisitions of inward purity as are outward sins to those for right conduct.

entries.title: Psalms 51:6
segments:
6. thou shalt make, &c.--may be taken to express God's gracious purpose in view of His strict requisition; a purpose of which David might have availed himself as a check to his native love for sin, and, in not doing so, aggravated his guilt. 
 
    truth ... and ...wisdom--are terms often used for piety (compare

entries.title: Psalms 51:7
segments:
7-12. A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. 
 
    Purge ... hyssop--The use of this plant in the ritual (
) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (

entries.title: Psalms 51:8
segments: 8. Make ... joy--by forgiving me, which will change distress to joy.

entries.title: Psalms 51:9
segments: 9. Hide, &c.--Turn from beholding.

entries.title: Psalms 51:10
segments:
10. Create--a work of almighty power. 
 
    in me--literally, "to me," or, "for me"; bestow as a gift, a heart free from taint of sin (

). 
 
    renew--implies that he had possessed it; the essential principle of a new nature had not been lost, but its influence interrupted (
); for
shows that he had not lost God's presence and Spirit (
), though he had lost the "joy of his salvation" (

), for whose return he prays. 
 
    right spirit--literally, "constant," "firm," not yielding to temptation.

entries.title: Psalms 51:12
segments: 12. free spirit--"thy" ought not to be supplied, for the word "free" is, literally, "willing," and "spirit" is that of David. "Let a willing spirit uphold me," that is, with a soul willingly conformed to God's law, he would be preserved in a right course of conduct.

entries.title: Psalms 51:13
segments:
13. Then--Such will be the effect of this gracious work.

entries.title: Psalms 51:15
segments: 15. open ... lips--by removing my sense of guilt.

entries.title: Psalms 51:16
segments: 16. Praise is better than sacrifice (
), and implying faith, penitence, and love, glorifies God. In true penitents the joys of pardon mingle with sorrow for sin.

entries.title: Psalms 51:18
segments:
18. Do good, &c.--Visit not my sin on Thy Church.
